 Safeguard Democracy
 Vote YES on Amendment 84 
 Joseph Repola , Student Contributor 
 November 2, 2026 
 Categories: 
 CO Ballot Measures 2026 
 Amendment 84 of Colorado’s constitution is increasing the security of mail-in election voting by requiring a form of ID to be added to mail-in ballots in addition to a signature. The proposed amendment would require one of the following to be included with the mail ballot: a Colorado REAL ID number, a Colorado REAL ID drivers license number, the last four digits of an ID that meets Colorado REAL ID standards, or the last four digits of a voter’s social security number. In regard to potential errors, the amendment states the County clerk or recorder may not count the ballot until the problem is fixed. Colorado voters are given 8 days to resubmit a mail ballot after being notified (Colorado Secretary of State, “2025-2026”). This amendment is an open and shut YES vote for Colorado citizens because currently the only way of verifying a ballot is with an affixed signature.
 Your right and responsibility to vote is granted to you as a citizen of the United States of America, so long as you are at least 18 years of age and are not a felon. As such with the staggering importance that voting carries with it, there should be checks in place to maintain the security and legitimacy of voting. As it currently stands, only a signature is required to be affixed to a mail-in ballot, with no additional identification required to request and return said ballot. This measure would bring Colorado to the forefront of 10 states that require ID to vote by mail, and distance Colorado from the 40 states that do not require any identification to vote by mail at all (“Colorado Amendment 84”).
 Amendment 84 provides a greater sense of security for Colorado voters knowing each ballot is tied to each voter expressing the right to vote. The term ‘Voter fraud’ has been used to delegitimize votes of the people of not just Colorado, but the nation. Even as recently as 2020 and 2024, vocal parties have claimed illegitimacy of voting due to mail-in ballots, with only 50% of Americans stating they were confident that elections are free, fair, and secure and 30% of Americans saying they have no confidence in voting (Confidence Poll). With current mail-in voting, signatures present on the ballot are compared to a signature on record, if a signature is even present at all. With the YES vote on Amendment 84, Colorado voters can rest assured that all votes cast come from the voter who cast it.
 An opposition party, The League of Women Voters of Colorado wrote, “It creates more hoops for voters and could lead to votes not being counted because of errors or omissions. It is a form of voter suppression” (“Colorado Amendment 84”). This group failed to read the final line of the amendment, which covers the possibility of errors, and voters being given the ability to rectify any mistakes on the ballot. The ‘hoops’ mentioned by the group is affixing an ID number to the outside envelope of your ballot, an ID more than likely on your person at this moment or within reach physically or electronically. This group would want you to believe this is a measure presented in bad faith by purposefully spreading lies that a clerical mistake would prevent you from voting.
 In addition, The Bell Policy Center states, “this measure creates barriers to voting for otherwise eligible citizens and will disproportionately disenfranchise already marginalized populations”(“Colorado Amendment 84”). This group reinforces harmful rhetoric that Colorado voters and marginalized subsets of the population are not intelligent enough, or have an inability to provide identification that nearly all Colorado citizens carry on a daily basis as well. This group wants you to think that voters are incapable or inept in providing identification with their ballot.
 Amendment 84 humbly started as a citizen-initiated ballot known as proposition number #362. As such, this proposition made it to the ballot box after enough petition signatures were collected to get onto the ballot. This is a measure generated by the people for the people. As of October 2026 the Colorado Voter Trust Initiative has consolidated 4.2 million dollars from donors to help secure Colorado voting. Prop #362 garnered 180,110 signatures of the 124,238 required signatures or 2% of Colorado voters to appear on the ballot (Colorado Secretary of State, “Committee Detail”).
 Your YES vote on amendment 84 prevents the unproductive grumbling of alleged voter fraud and ensures that all future elections held in this great state of Colorado are fair, free, and secure for today, tomorrow, and forever. With your YES vote, you can rest assured that you did your part in creating a better voting environment for all of Colorado. If you have made it to the end of this editorial with a NO on 84, you carry the responsibility of diluting the strength of your own vote and the votes of your community.
 Vote YES on amendment 84. It’s your right to protect democracy.
 Works Cited
“Colorado Amendment 84, Require Voter Identification Number for Mail-In Ballots Initiative
(2026).” Ballotpedia, https://ballotpedia.org/Colorado_Amendment_84,_Require_Voter_Identification_Number 
_for_Mail-In_Ballots_Initiative_(2026). Accessed 21 Oct. 2026.
